entry.title: A wider circle of familiar people
entry.summary: Both books describe family life among relatives, friends, caregivers, and people in the neighborhood. The Baby authors recognize that parenting can feel isolated and invite families to build connections from the people available to them.
entry.cue: When you want company or familiar connections beyond the people at home.
detail: This circle can include friends with children and friends with whom you talk about other interests. The Baby authors also name neighbors and people in local shops whose faces become familiar through everyday life.
For relatives who live far away, they suggest sharing books, songs, or music over a video call, with in-person visits when possible. It is one way to stay connected across distance.
Davies includes relatives and people who are not related to you within the family’s wider community. These are possibilities for connection, not a list of relationships every family must maintain.

references.locator: Isolation and varied connections: near and distant relatives, friends, neighbors and local people

displayContext.footer: You don’t need a different home. Start with what you have.
